name: settlement
description: Communities, strongholds, camps, and population centers

entries.value: Farming Hamlet — twenty families clustered around a well, shrine, granary, and communal oven.
Crossroads Village — inns, stables, traders, and craftspeople serving traffic from three roads.
Fishing Village — boats, smokehouses, net sheds, and homes raised against seasonal floods.
Walled Market Town — a prosperous regional center with gates, guilds, taxes, and crowded suburbs.
Mining Town — rough housing and busy foundries beneath a wealthy company office and dangerous shafts.
Pilgrim Town — hostels, relic sellers, healers, and rival temples surrounding a sacred destination.
Frontier Fort — soldiers, settlers, workshops, and refugees sheltered behind unfinished defenses.
Adventurer Camp — tents, supply stalls, healers, mercenaries, and rumor boards beside unexplored ruins.
Hill Castle — a noble household and garrison overlooking farms gathered beneath its protection.
River Port — warehouses, ferries, shipyards, customs officers, and floating neighborhoods.
Coastal City — fortified harbors, foreign quarters, naval yards, markets, and competing merchant families.
Monastery Community — monks, tenant farmers, guests, libraries, and workshops behind peaceful walls.
Nomad Encampment — mobile homes, livestock enclosures, craft tents, and a council fire.
Forest Enclave — homes integrated into living trees and protected by scouts who control every path.
Mountain Hold — a fortified underground settlement built around mines, cisterns, and ancestral halls.
Island Commune — a self-sufficient harbor settlement governed through public meetings and shared labor.
Royal Capital — palace districts, ministries, slums, universities, barracks, and constant political theater.
Free City — an independent trade metropolis balancing guilds, foreign powers, and citizen factions.
Floating Settlement — boats and platforms permanently lashed together around a deep-water anchorage.
Underground Refuge — descendants of disaster survivors living around finite water, light, and old machinery.
Ruined City Camp — scavengers and scholars occupying defensible blocks of a much larger dead metropolis.
Siege Camp — a temporary city of soldiers, engineers, merchants, prisoners, disease, and competing commanders.
